name: AI Agent
label: AI Agent
description: Multimodal agent orchestrator (templateId 5c8b0d45-1d10-4f2e-844c-2318af96b2f1). Accepts text plus image/audio/video/document attachments on INPUT main_input, calls the connected LLM on FUNCTION model, fans out to connected tools / sub-agents / data sources, emits the final answer plus generated media on OUTPUT main_output, and publishes live reasoning and tool-dispatch events on FUNCTION thoughts. The model request is {messages, tools} plus optional inputFiles; the model may return outputFiles. The handler prefers helper executeStream for that call and falls back to atomic execute when executeStream is missing or returns a non-stream result; provider envelopes (result / response / llm_output / output / data / value, and one-element lists) are unwrapped to the canonical assistant payload. Preserves v1 dynamics: edge-time tool name + description, alias-resolved tool/sub-agent dispatch, diff-synced cross-run remote memory (preserving tool calls and tool outputs across turns without duplicating full chat history), on-demand RAG over connected data sources (never pre-fetched blindly at turn start), wrapper response merge, and the Anthropic-strict every-tool_use-has-a-tool_result invariant. conversation_id is scoped internally from the execution context (or a fresh UUID when non-conversational) and is never exposed on main_input or main_output. A missing model connection fails the run with RuntimeError. Example main_input: {"prompt":"Where is order 42?","files":[{"kind":"image","mime_type":"image/jpeg","source":"base64","data":"/9j/…","name":"label.jpg"}]}. Data protection: prompts, attachments, and conversation context leave this host to the configured model provider (GDPR/data-processing notice). Secrets belong only in configurationParameters and are never logged.
author: c525bb64-f52e-4829-8bf0-f1fe33aa6b42

ports.name: model
ports.description: Connect exactly one v2 LLM provider (OpenAI Models, Local LLM, or another node that speaks the same contract). REQUIRED at runtime even though required=false in the designer: zero connections raise 'Missing required LLM connection on `model` FUNCTION port.' maxConnections=1. The agent sends node_request {messages: <canonical history>, tools: <tool catalog including delegate_to_agent when sub_agents exist>, inputFiles?: <ContentBlocks from main_input.files + main_input.voices>} so the provider can emitPartial thinking/answer deltas. Non-empty files+voices are sent as top-level inputFiles (omitted when empty). The provider may return outputFiles; the agent merges those with result.output_files. Invoke path: helper executeStream(portValue='model', …) first; if executeStream is not available on the helper, throws, or returns a non-stream/empty body, the agent falls back to atomic execute(portValue='model', …) and waits for one envelope. Response unwrap (recursive, depth≤10): one-element lists are peeled; dict envelopes are opened in order result, response, llm_output, output, data, value; a dict with role=='assistant' or keys tool_calls|thinking|thoughts|output_files|finish_reason|error is the payload. Empty transport ([], null, '', [{}]) is a terminal provider-return-path error (not retried — side effects such as image generation already happened). Example request: {"messages":[{"role":"system","content":"You are a packer."},{"role":"user","content":"Where is order 42?"}],"tools":[{"name":"lookup_order","description":"Fetch an order.","request":{"type":"object","properties":{"id":{"type":"string"}}}}],"stream":true}.

inputSchema.label: messages
inputSchema.description: Conversation history the provider must complete. Purpose: built by the agent from system (role+instructions+STRICT_TOOL_CALL_RULES+on-demand DATA_SOURCE_RAG_RULES when data tools are wired), diff-synced prior memory, and the current user turn. Accepted value: list of {role, content, tool_calls?, thinking?, thoughts?, tool_call_id?, name?}. content is a string or a list of typed blocks (text/image/audio/video/document/tool_use/tool_result). MULTIMODAL FILES travel here: main_input.files are hoisted into the latest user message as {type:'image'|'audio'|'video'|'document', …} blocks. Omit is illegal at runtime (the agent always sends at least system+user). Example: [{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Read this PDF."},{"type":"document","mime_type":"application/pdf","source":"base64","data":"JVBERi0…","name":"spec.pdf"}]}].

inputSchema.label: tools
inputSchema.description: Tool catalog the provider should advertise this round. Purpose: built from DuckTape mappings on the tools and data FUNCTION ports plus a synthetic delegate_to_agent when sub_agent is connected. Accepted value: list of {name, description, request:<JSON Schema>}. Empty list is valid (no tools). The provider translates to its native shape (OpenAI function-tool, Anthropic input_schema, etc.). Example: [{"name":"delegate_to_agent","description":"Hand a task to a connected sub-agent.","request":{"type":"object","properties":{"agent_id":{"type":"string"},"prompt":{"type":"string"}},"required":["agent_id","prompt"]}}].

inputSchema.label: inputFiles
inputSchema.description: user-uploaded files and voice clips for the model

outputSchema.label: result
outputSchema.description: Canonical assistant payload after envelope unwrap. Purpose: drives the tool loop and the final main_output. Accepted shape: {role:'assistant', content:[<ContentBlock>], tool_calls?:[{id, name, args, type:'tool_call'}], thoughts?:[{type, text, signature?}], thinking?: <legacy mirror>, output_files?:[<ContentBlock>], finish_reason?, usage?, error?}. The agent also accepts this object at the top level (no result wrapper) and inside result/response/llm_output/output/data/value. Empty content with no tool_calls/output_files/thoughts is retried up to 2 times unless finish_reason is a terminal failure (error, content_filter, refusal, safety, blocked). Example: {"role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Packed."}],"finish_reason":"stop"}.

ports.name: memory
ports.description: Optional remote conversation memory (maxConnections=1). Purpose: persist full execution turns (including tool calls and tool outputs) across runs on a GENERIC cache node (Redis Cache, or any node whose INPUT speaks SET/GET/DEL/RPUSH/LRANGE/LTRIM). The agent scopes the key as sq:memory:<workflowId:nodeId:conversationId> (or a fresh UUID for non-conversational runs), reads existing history via LRANGE 0 -1, compares it against the incoming full chat thread, trims/clears on prompt-edit divergence (LTRIM/DEL), and appends only the new diff turns via RPUSH — never duplicating prior chat messages. conversation_id is never taken from main_input or written to main_output. Unconnected → in-process cache. Remote failures log a warning and fall back to in-memory. Responses unwrap from value / data.value / history / matches lists (JSON strings are parsed). Example append: {"operation":"RPUSH","key":"sq:memory:wf1:node1:conv1","value":{"role":"user","content":"Where is order 42?"}}.

inputSchema.label: operation
inputSchema.description: Generic cache verb the agent emits. Purpose: the connected cache node branches on this through its normal INPUT.operation (or an alias the mapper projects onto: command/op). EXACT values this agent sends: 'RPUSH' (append one serialized turn) | 'LRANGE' (read the conversation list) | 'LTRIM' (trim diverged suffix) | 'DEL' (clear before reset/compaction). Never 'add_message' or 'get_history'. Omit is not used. Example append: 'RPUSH'. Example read: 'LRANGE'.

inputSchema.label: key
inputSchema.description: Cache key for this agent's conversation history. Purpose: persist across turns of the same conversation while isolating different workflows and sibling/sub-agents. Accepted value: 'sq:memory:' plus scoped workflowId:nodeId:conversationId (or internal uuid4 when non-conversational). Never read from main_input or written to main_output. Example: 'sq:memory:wf1:agent1:9f1c6d2e-4a11-4b22-8c33-77aa00bbcc11'.

inputSchema.label: value
inputSchema.description: Serialized turn stored when operation='RPUSH'. Purpose: append one canonical message. Accepted shape: {role, content, tool_calls?, …} after normalizeMessageForStorage. Omitted on LRANGE/LTRIM/DEL. The peer may persist this as JSON. Example: {"role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Order 42 is in bin A."}]}.

inputSchema.label: start
inputSchema.description: Inclusive list index for operation='LRANGE' or 'LTRIM'. Purpose: window or trim the remote list; the agent sends 0. Accepted values: integers. Default 0. Negative indexes follow Redis (from the tail). Example: 0.

inputSchema.label: stop
inputSchema.description: Inclusive list end for operation='LRANGE' (-1) or 'LTRIM' (keepCount - 1). Accepted values: integers. -1 means the last element on Redis-style lists. Example: -1.

inputSchema.label: ttl_seconds
inputSchema.description: Optional key TTL in seconds. Purpose: forwarded only when the peer schema declares ttl_seconds/ttl AND this value is a positive integer. Accepted values: integers ≥ 1 to expire; 0 / omit / negative → no TTL field is sent (peer default). This agent currently omits TTL (0). Example: 86400.

outputSchema.label: status
outputSchema.description: Peer success flag. Purpose: 'ok' means the cache op completed. EXACT accepted values the agent treats as success: 'ok'. Missing/other values still unwrap value/data when present. Example: 'ok'.

outputSchema.label: value
outputSchema.description: LRANGE result: list of canonical message dicts or JSON strings of the same shape (oldest first when the peer is RPUSH). Purpose: the agent normalizes each element into history. Empty/missing → []. Also accepted envelopes: data.value, data.history, history, result.history. Example: [{"role":"user","content":"hi"}].

outputSchema.label: error
outputSchema.description: Failure message from the cache node. Purpose: a non-empty error is treated as a remote failure and the agent falls back to in-memory. Never contains secrets. Empty/omit on success. Example: 'connection timed out'.

ports.name: data
ports.description: Optional data sources for on-demand RAG retrieval (maxConnections=0 means unbounded). Purpose: every connected GENERIC vector-DB / search node (PGVector, Pinecone, Chroma, Qdrant, or any compatible INPUT schema) is exposed to the LLM as a callable RAG search tool ({query, topK?}). Pre-RAG at conversation/turn start is NOT performed; instead the agent decides relevant search keywords and queries connected data tools on demand before answering. The agent maps tool calls onto the peer's declared fields (operation/QUERY, query, embedding?, topK, filter). Example call: {"operation":"QUERY","query":"order 42 warehouse location","topK":5,"filter":{}}.

inputSchema.label: operation
inputSchema.description: Generic vector-DB verb the agent emits. Purpose: mapped onto the peer INPUT.operation (or command/op). EXACT value this agent sends: 'QUERY' (similarity search). The mapper remaps to a peer-declared synonym when the peer schema lists vector.query | collection.query | collection.search | entities.search | query | search. Never a custom 'addMessage' / node-specific RAG command. Omit is not used by this agent. Example: 'QUERY'. Example after remap onto Pinecone: 'vector.query'.

inputSchema.label: query
inputSchema.description: Free-text keyword or semantic retrieval query. Purpose: filled by the model's tool args when the LLM calls the data source as an on-demand RAG tool (the LLM-facing catalog exposes {query:string, topK?:integer}). Accepted value: any string. Example: 'invoice 8831 line items'.

inputSchema.label: embedding
inputSchema.description: Query vector for similarity search. Purpose: forwarded when the model or an upstream embedder supplied embedding/vector/query_embeddings; omitted when empty so text-only peers can embed themselves. Accepted value: number[] (finite floats). A nested [[...]] from Chroma-style query_embeddings is flattened to one vector. Do not log. Example: [0.12, -0.04, 0.88].

inputSchema.label: topK
inputSchema.description: Neighbor count for the similarity query. Purpose: default 5 when the model omits it. Accepted values: integers ≥ 1. Non-positive / blank / non-numeric → 5. Mapped onto peer fields topK | top_k | n_results | limit | k. Example: 5. Example for a narrow lookup: 3.

inputSchema.label: filter
inputSchema.description: Optional metadata filter passed through to the vector store. Purpose: restrict neighbors (tenant, collection, tag). Accepted value: JSON object. Empty {} is sent when the peer declares filter/where/metadata_filter. Mapped onto filter | where | metadata_filter. Example: {"source":"orders"}.

inputSchema.label: name
inputSchema.description: Optional data-source tool name shown to the LLM. Purpose: read from the connection edge (DuckTape sourcePath=name); if omitted, synthesized automatically from the connected node's name so the source is always callable for RAG. NOT sent on the wire to the peer. Example: 'orders_kb'.

inputSchema.label: description
inputSchema.description: Optional when-to-call text shown to the LLM. Purpose: read from the connection edge; if omitted, a default RAG search description is synthesized automatically. NOT sent on the wire to the peer. Example: 'Search internal order records by order id or customer name.'.

outputSchema.label: status
outputSchema.description: Peer success flag. Purpose: 'ok' means retrieval completed. EXACT accepted success value: 'ok'. Missing/other values still unwrap matches/documents when present. Example: 'ok'.

outputSchema.label: matches
outputSchema.description: Retrieved neighbors returned to the model as a tool result. Accepted value: list of objects or strings ({id?, document|text|title?, score?, metadata?}). Also accepted envelopes: documents, value, data.matches, data.value, result, response. Example: [{"id":"42","document":"Order 42 is in bin A-12","score":0.91}].

outputSchema.label: error
outputSchema.description: Failure message from the data node. Returned to the model as a tool error message so it can refine or proceed. Never contains secrets. Empty/omit on success. Example: 'collection not found'.

ports.name: tools
ports.description: Generic tool hub (unbounded connections). Purpose: each connection carries DuckTape mapping; the agent reads the user-written name + description on the connection edge and builds JSON Schema properties from mappings whose sourcePath is 'request' (targetPath = the target node's input field). Resolver order for a model-emitted tool name: exact > alias_exact > alias_contains > alias_tokens. The wrapper request/response shape is preserved across the call (_merge_wrapper_dict). Duplicate (name, args) pairs in one run return a cached-style tool_result instead of re-invoking. Anthropic-strict: every tool_use gets a tool_result even on error. Example dispatch payload: {"request":{"order_id":"42"},"name":"lookup_order","description":"Fetch an order by id."}.

inputSchema.label: request
inputSchema.description: DuckTape wrapper holding the tool's actual parameters. Purpose: children come from the edge mapping (sourcePath=request → targetPath=<field>). The agent fills those fields from the model's tool_call args. Omit/empty → tool is invoked with an empty request object. Example child mapping: request.order_id → lookup_order.order_id with value '42'.

inputSchema.label: name
inputSchema.description: Tool display name. Purpose: read by the agent from the connection edge (DuckTape sourcePath=name). This is the name the LLM must emit. Empty name drops the connection from the catalog. Example: 'lookup_order'.

inputSchema.label: description
inputSchema.description: Tool description exposed to the LLM. Purpose: read from the connection edge. Empty description drops the connection from the catalog. Example: 'Return the warehouse bin for an order id.'.

outputSchema.label: response
outputSchema.description: DuckTape wrapper holding the tool's return values (children from the edge mapping). Purpose: merged into the tool_result content the agent appends to history. The handler also accepts a bare object/list/string after unwrap. Example: {"bin":"A-12","status":"packed"}.

ports.name: sub_agent
ports.description: Sub-agent collaboration hub. Purpose: the master exposes a synthetic tool delegate_to_agent whose agent_id.enum is the connected node ids. Sub-agent connection-detail configurationParameters (role / instructions / prompt) win over master-supplied overrides. v2 forwards files attachments. conversation_id is NEVER passed — every agent creates its own internal memory id; if the master needs the sub-agent to know prior context, it must embed that context in prompt (or files). Unconnected → no delegate_to_agent tool. Ambiguous/missing agent_id returns a tool_result error listing available ids. Example payload: {"role":"Researcher","instructions":"Cite sources.","prompt":"Summarize the attached PDF for the packer.","files":[{"kind":"document","mime_type":"application/pdf","source":"base64","data":"JVBERi0…","name":"spec.pdf"}]}.

inputSchema.label: role
inputSchema.description: Optional role override sent to the sub-agent's main_input. Purpose: sub-agent's own config role wins when set; otherwise this value; otherwise the sub-agent default. Accepted value: non-empty string. Empty → omitted from the payload. Example: 'Warehouse researcher'.

inputSchema.label: instructions
inputSchema.description: Optional instructions override. Purpose: sub-agent's own config instructions win when set. Empty → omitted. Example: 'Only use the attached spec. If unknown, say so.'.

inputSchema.label: prompt
inputSchema.description: Task content. Purpose: master connection-detail prompt (if any) is concatenated with the model-supplied prompt/input/task/text/content (newline-separated). This is the only way to pass prior conversation — do not send conversation_id. Empty after merge → payload may omit prompt and the sub-agent runs on its own config prompt only. Example: 'Find bin for order 42. Prior turn: customer asked for ETA.'.

inputSchema.label: files
inputSchema.description: Optional multimodal attachments forwarded from the master. Purpose: copied from delegate_to_agent args.files when it is a non-empty list. Accepted value: list of {kind:'image'|'audio'|'video'|'document', mime_type, source:'base64'|'url'|'file_id', data, name?}. Omit/[] → not sent. Example: [{"kind":"image","mime_type":"image/png","source":"base64","data":"iVBOR…","name":"label.png"}]. Prefer source:'file_id' (platform file reference) over inline base64 for large payloads.

outputSchema.label: final_answer
outputSchema.description: Sub-agent's final-answer text (the same field the sub-agent emits on its own main_output). Purpose: unwrapped from list envelopes and placed in the master's tool_result content. Empty string if the sub-agent returned no text. Example: 'Order 42 is in bin A-12.'.

outputSchema.label: output_files
outputSchema.description: Optional generated media from the sub-agent (image/audio/video/document content blocks). Purpose: forwarded into the master's history/tool_result when present. Omit/[] when none. Example: [{"type":"image","mime_type":"image/png","source":"base64","data":"iVBOR…"}]. Generated media is emitted as platform file references (file_id) whenever possible.

ports.name: main_input
ports.description: Agent input (unbounded connections merged). Purpose: getInputValuesByPortValue('main_input') — each list item is a string (treated as prompt) or an object {role?, instructions?, prompt?, files?}. Priority: prompt ALWAYS merges config prompt + every connection (newline-joined); role → config wins, else joined connection roles, else 'You are a helpful AI assistant.'; instructions → config wins, else joined connection instructions, else ''; files → concatenated across connections. Empty incoming with empty config prompt still runs (user turn may be blank; the LLM receives role+instructions only). Example: {"prompt":"Where is order 42?","files":[{"kind":"image","mime_type":"image/jpeg","source":"base64","data":"/9j/…","name":"label.jpg"}]}.

schema.label: role
schema.description: Optional role override for this invocation. Purpose: used only when configurationParameter role is blank/whitespace. Multiple connections are newline-joined. Accepted value: non-empty string. Example: 'You are a warehouse copilot.'.

schema.label: instructions
schema.description: Optional instructions override. Purpose: used only when configurationParameter instructions is blank. Multiple connections are newline-joined. STRICT_TOOL_CALL_RULES are still appended by the agent. Example: 'Never invent bin locations. Call lookup_order.'.

schema.label: prompt
schema.description: User prompt / task content. Purpose: always concatenated with configurationParameter prompt (config first) and every other connected prompt, newline-joined. A bare string input is treated as this field. Conversation mode: the Duckbot start msg port delivers the whole thread here as a JSON array string of {role, content} messages — the agent expands it into role-tagged history (last entry = current turn). Empty → no user text (files-only turns are still valid). Example: 'Pack order 42 and say which bin.'.

schema.label: files
schema.description: Optional multimodal attachments hoisted into the latest user message as content blocks. Purpose: _coerce_files_list accepts a list, a single dict, or a JSON/Python-literal string. Each item: {kind:'image'|'audio'|'video'|'document' (default document), mime_type (or mimeType, default application/octet-stream), source:'base64'|'url'|'file_id', data, name?}. Base64 data may include a data:<mime>;base64, prefix. Omit/[] → text-only. Example: [{"kind":"document","mime_type":"application/pdf","source":"base64","data":"JVBERi0…","name":"bol.pdf"}]. Prefer source:'file_id' (platform file reference) over inline base64 for large payloads.

ports.name: main_output
ports.description: Agent's final answer. Purpose: returnResult ResultItem('main_output', {final_answer, output_files, voices}). final_answer is the text extracted from the last assistant payload's content blocks; output_files is that payload's output_files list (or []); voices is the audio subset of output_files (kind/type audio or mime_type audio/*, still kept in output_files; empty list when none). Thoughts are NOT on this port — they were already published live on FUNCTION thoughts. conversation_id is intentionally absent. On uncaught exception the handler still emits main_output with an error string in final_answer. Example: {"final_answer":"Order 42 is in bin A-12.","output_files":[],"voices":[]}.

schema.label: final_answer
schema.description: Plain-text final answer extracted from the last assistant content (text blocks concatenated). Purpose: the only text downstream nodes should show as the agent reply. Empty string if the model returned only tool calls that never resolved to text (should be rare after the loop). On handler failure: the exception message. Example: 'Packed onto pallet 7.'.

schema.label: output_files
schema.description: Generated media copied from the last assistant payload's output_files (image/audio/video/document content blocks produced by the model, e.g. dall-e via OpenAI Models). Purpose: pass bytes/refs downstream without putting them in final_answer. Missing/non-list → []. Example: [{"type":"image","mime_type":"image/png","source":"base64","data":"iVBOR…","name":"bin-map.png"}]. Generated media is emitted as platform file references (file_id) whenever possible.

ports.name: thoughts
ports.description: Live reasoning stream of the agent. Purpose: publishes the agent's thinking text as it runs — live deltas via emitPartial(port='thoughts', channel='thinking') that the daemon routes along this port's edges (through any edge JOLT) to whatever node is wired here (Duckbot end renders it as the thinking bubble; a thinking-store node would persist it), plus one assembled execute per thinking block carrying a single {thoughts: text} payload. Tool-dispatch notices are published the same way as human-readable text. If nothing is connected, events are silently dropped (observability never fails the agent). Unwired thoughts port = no live thinking (the graph decides, never a bypass). Example assembled payload: {"thoughts":"I should look up order 42."}.

inputSchema.label: thoughts
inputSchema.description: The agent's live reasoning text. Purpose: the ONLY value published on this port — one emit per thinking block (and per tool-dispatch notice, as human-readable text) while the agent runs, plus live deltas via emitPartial(port='thoughts', channel='thinking'). Downstream nodes (e.g. a Duckbot end msg input or a thinking store) consume this text directly; there is no event envelope, no iteration index, no signature, no tool_calls structure on the wire. Empty when the model produced no reasoning. Example: 'I should look up order 42 before answering.'.

configurationParameters.label: Name
configurationParameters.description: Default agent name/role injected as the core system message. Purpose: wins over any role on main_input when this value is a non-empty string (after strip). Empty/whitespace → use merged main_input roles, else 'You are a helpful AI assistant.'. Accepted value: free text. Example: 'Agent Maygent'. Example override-disabled (blank so the port wins): ''.

configurationParameters.label: Instructions
configurationParameters.description: Default agent instructions appended after role in the core system message (STRICT_TOOL_CALL_RULES are still added by the handler). Purpose: wins over main_input.instructions when this is non-empty. Empty → use merged port instructions. Accepted value: free text, including markdown. Example: 'You pack warehouse orders. Call lookup_order before answering. Never invent a bin.'.

configurationParameters.label: Prompt
configurationParameters.description: Static prompt prefix concatenated with every prompt arriving on main_input (config first, then port values, newline-joined). Purpose: standing task text that should apply to every run of this instance. Empty → only port prompts are used. Not a substitute for instructions. Example: 'Customer timezone: America/New_York.'.

configurationParameters.label: Max Iterations
configurationParameters.description: Maximum tool-call loop iterations after the first LLM round. Purpose: int(str(value) or 10) — caps how many times the agent will dispatch tools and call the model again. Accepted values: integers ≥ 0. Default: 10. 0 means the first model response is final even if it contains tool_calls (those calls are not executed). Non-numeric strings raise at int() and fail the node. Example: 10. Example for a shallow router: 2.

configurationParameters.label: Context Window (tokens)
configurationParameters.description: Maximum tokens the agent will send to the LLM in one round (local estimate: chars/4). Purpose: when the history estimate exceeds this number, the agent compacts in two steps: (A) collapse every non-system, non-summary message into ONE new system-role 'Summarized((…))' block after existing summaries — only the first core system message (role + instructions + STRICT_TOOL_CALL_RULES) is preserved verbatim; (B) if still over, re-summarize all summary blocks into ONE meta-summary so history is [core system] + [one Summarized((…))]. Each summary block carries Summarized((…)) plus _summarized=true and _summary_kind=summarized_chat_history. A 'summary' event is published on thoughts when compaction happens. Accepted values: integers. Default: 200000. 0, blank, or non-numeric → treated as 200000 except 0 after a successful int parse disables summarization (oversized requests then fail at the provider). Set 0 only if you accept provider context_length_exceeded errors. Example: 200000. Example disable: 0.
